analysis.title: Global Markets Outlook 2027: Growing Pains
key_insights: GS baseline for 2027 is stable global growth, declining inflation and peaking policy rates, but market risks skew to the downside as the market cycle ages. Higher real rates, wider credit spreads and rising under-the-surface volatility are the late-cycle headwinds, on top of the Iran war energy shock.

The AI investment impulse (additional AI investment as a share of GDP) is forecast to peak in early 2027, with the peak in the investment share itself in 2028. This is manageable for the economy but a bigger test for markets, because AI has contributed more to earnings and market value growth than to GDP growth.

Companies levered to AI infrastructure have de-rated significantly since June, after being the biggest market beneficiaries in 1H 2026. The market focus has moved from valuation excess to the sustainability of record profits, with S&P 500 earnings at a record share of GDP.
GS expects S&P 500 earnings growth to slow from 36% in 2026 to 11% in 2027. That limits the de-rating in AI-exposed areas but implies less relief in core rates pricing.

Equity gains may pass from AI infrastructure to hyperscalers (if monetization becomes visible), AI-productivity beneficiaries, and non-AI companies as crowding out of capital eases. The risk is that the rotation becomes a larger aggregate shock if markets look ahead to the 2028 peak, the handoff is slow, or financial and credit conditions tighten in a feedback loop. Financial conditions are the most likely channel for AI worries to hit the economy.

An escalation-driven oil spike from the Iran war is one of the largest near-term risks. It would hurt equities, support the Dollar against European currencies and push rates higher. Europe is vulnerable this winter given low natural gas storage.

GS baseline is a gradual decline in energy prices even without full resolution of the conflict. Oil supply has largely been restored, but the market has demanded a fluctuating risk premium above fundamentals. The premium fell recently, which raises the hedge value of energy. When it was very high at end-October, outright longs were riskier than options.
Faster resolution of Iran or Ukraine is among the clearest upside risks for broader markets, since lower energy prices would support both bonds and equities.

GS sees central bank pricing in the US and UK as too hawkish versus its baseline. Policy rates should peak lower than in 2023-2024 and reverse earlier, with the Fed moving from hikes to cuts in late 2027 and early 2028. Risk to the view: the energy shock extends or inflation stays sticky with a resilient labour market.

GS argues for higher bond allocations: good running yield and a spread to cash, cheap valuations (UST 10y at 4.6% by end-2027) with underweight positioning, and stress from higher real rates that is hard to sustain. Bonds are regaining hedge value as supply shocks give way to demand stresses (Bunds rallied as French spreads widened; USTs rallied as tech fell).

GS forecasts a roughly 3% fall in the broad trade-weighted Dollar in 2027 as US inflation converges to target, energy prices fall and the Fed turns to cuts. The key swing factor is whether the AI peak erodes US equity returns and the cross-border equity inflows that support the Dollar's premium valuation.

If US tech performance erodes, GS expects cyclical Dollar underperformance rather than a safe-haven bid, with the undervalued Yen the better haven. Japanese authorities are focused on limiting Yen weakness. GS also sees further gradual CNY appreciation on a growing trade surplus and deep undervaluation that forwards underestimate.

Europe faces energy terms-of-trade pressure, higher global yields and French sovereign stress that is unlikely to be addressed until the French election in spring 2027. Low carry and skewed risks keep downside optionality in EUR attractive. Europe's small tech share could look relatively better in an AI slowdown.

UK: Gilts have the highest beta to oil and could be the clearest DM rates outperformers if oil falls. UK equities are defensive with low tech exposure but significant energy exposure. Sterling is the most overvalued G10 currency and GS's UK monetary policy forecasts are the most dovish relative to market pricing, so further gains are harder.

Credit and equity issuance are at cycle records and likely to grow in 2027 with AI financing needs. AI-related credits have underperformed over the last six months. GS expects modest further widening in US index-level credit spreads, with risks skewed to wider, plus modest US HY underperformance (decompression) and episodic indigestion from jumbo AI debt deals.

Europe offers more credit risk premium than the US, and mortgages and structured credit offer refuge from heavy corporate supply. GS thinks a 1998-2000 style sustained spread widening and credit-equity decoupling is harder to repeat without EM-crisis capital inflows and goods deflation.

EM was resilient again in 2026 (EM equities on track for a double-digit year after 30% gains in 2025), but local rate spreads are tight, EM credit spreads are the tightest in years and FX carry and valuations are middling. GS favours exposure to high, diversified yields in hard- and local-currency EM fixed income (South Africa, Hungary, Colombia, India) and to diversified EM equity earnings, especially equal-weighted indices.

Tail hedging: GS favours positioning for lower rates in the US and Japan, or lower rates and equities together, and USD/JPY downside. For energy it favours European gas futures and TTF call spreads and EUR funding. In equities it favours out-of-the-money puts or replacing holdings with longer-dated calls. Index volatility is unlikely to fall much and has scope to rise if stresses broaden.
GS baseline forecasts positive 2027 returns for both equities and bonds, but stresses diversification across bonds, commodities (especially energy) and equity selection.

sector_views.rationale: Earnings growth stays positive, but the investment impulse peaks in early 2027 and the group has already de-rated since June.
Gains could pass to hyperscalers if monetization paths become more visible, but free cash flow has deteriorated sharply.
Defensive with less tech exposure than the US, though with significant energy exposure.
Under pressure from global shocks and French stress, but a small tech share may look relatively better in an AI slowdown.
Diversified earnings mix across tech in North Asia, cyclicals in South Africa and LatAm, and domestic demand in India. Equal-weighted indices preferred.
Heavy AI-related issuance needs discounted pricing, and risks skew to wider spreads.
Higher running yield, cheap valuations, underweight positioning and better hedge value.
Baseline is a gradual decline in prices, but energy is a valuable hedge against escalation.

earnings_insights: GS expects S&P 500 earnings growth of 36% in 2026 (forecast) slowing to 11% in 2027 (forecast). S&P 500 earnings are at a record share of GDP.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS sees valuations as cheap with scope for shallow rate relief, and more if AI spending decelerates faster.
A slower but still robust pace limits de-rating but offers less relief for core rates.
Lower US inflation, lower energy prices and Fed cuts support a softer Dollar.

macro_indicators.reading: hikes to cuts in late 2027 and early 2028
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS sees market pricing in the US and UK as too hawkish.
A second-derivative peak that markets may treat as a limit on upside. The investment share itself peaks in 2028.

macro_indicators.reading: gradual decline in baseline, with risks skewed to the upside
macro_indicators.interpretation: The risk premium fell recently, which raises the hedge value of energy.

trade_ideas.description: Position for lower US and Japanese rates, or for jointly lower rates and equities, as protection against downside growth tails
trade_ideas.rationale: A growing number of risks (AI reversal, cybersecurity fears, AI-related labour shedding, financial stress) would push growth and rate expectations lower.
trade_ideas.risk: Oil spikes or sticky core inflation would push rates higher.

trade_ideas.description: Long USD/JPY downside (short USD/JPY) as a hedge
trade_ideas.rationale: USD/JPY generally performs well when rates and equities are both falling, and Japanese authorities are limiting Yen weakness.

trade_ideas.description: European gas futures and TTF call spreads, and EUR funding, as asymmetric energy hedges
trade_ideas.rationale: Europe has low gas storage and faces supply and weather risks this winter.

trade_ideas.description: Out-of-the-money equity index puts, or replace equity holdings with longer-dated call options
trade_ideas.rationale: Protection is more valuable than usual as the cycle matures and index volatility has scope to rise.
French sovereign stress persists until the spring 2027 election, with skewed risks and low carry.
trade_ideas.risk: Relief in energy or global yields could help the Euro.

trade_ideas.description: Long JPY and CNY versus USD
trade_ideas.rationale: Yen is undervalued and a better haven if US tech erodes. CNY is undervalued with a growing trade surplus and forwards underestimate appreciation.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight duration in DM government bonds, particularly UK Gilts if oil falls
trade_ideas.rationale: Running yield, cheap valuations, underweight positioning and hedge value. Gilts have the highest beta to oil.
trade_ideas.risk: The energy shock extends further or inflation remains sticky with a resilient labour market.

trade_ideas.description: EM local and hard-currency fixed income and equal-weighted EM equities
trade_ideas.rationale: High, diversified and resilient yields, and a regionally diversified earnings mix.
trade_ideas.risk: Tight spreads and middling carry and valuations after 2026 outperformance.

risk_factors: Escalation in the Iran war driving an oil price spike, which could hit equities and bonds together.
Peak in the AI investment impulse becoming a larger aggregate market shock if markets look ahead to the 2028 peak.
Rotation out of AI infrastructure into other sectors not happening quickly or smoothly enough.
Feedback loops from tighter financial and credit conditions.
Record credit and equity issuance causing indigestion, with jumbo AI debt deals widening spreads.
Sticky core inflation or a resilient labour market keeping central banks hawkish.
French sovereign and fiscal stress until the spring 2027 election.
European winter gas supply and weather risk with low storage.
Erosion of US tech exceptionalism, weakening the Dollar's premium valuation.
Cybersecurity fears and AI-related labour shedding as growth risks.
Weaker borrowers in the left tail of credit creating more turbulent financing conditions.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 shows the AI contribution to growth in US GDP, capex, earnings and market value, with values labelled 21, 62, 62, 92 and 41 percent across US GDP, US Capex, US Earnings, US Market Value (Peak) and US Market Value (YTD). The mapping of values to categories is inferred from the axis order in the text.
Exhibit 2 plots S&P 500 total earnings as a share of GDP (4-quarter moving average) from 1995 with a linear trend line, and the text says it is a record share.
vol_and_positioning: Equity index volatility has risen a little but is unlikely to fall much and has scope to rise if macro stresses broaden. The sharpest volatility so far is under the surface of the major indices.
Deeper equity protection via out-of-the-money puts, or replacing equity holdings with longer-dated call options, looks more valuable than usual as the cycle matures.
Bond positioning is underweight, per GS.
Using the Euro as a funder for other crosses has been a popular position. Skew and low carry make EUR downside optionality attractive.
Energy hedges: European gas futures and TTF call spreads, and EUR funding, as asymmetric protection.
When the oil risk premium is very high (as at end-October), outright longs rather than options have been riskier.
geopolitical: Iran war: escalation could cause an oil spike. Oil supply has largely been restored despite the ongoing war.
Ukraine: faster resolution is an upside risk for markets through lower energy prices.
French election in spring 2027: French fiscal issues are unlikely to be addressed until then, keeping EUR downside attractive.
Europe winter energy risk: low natural gas storage leaves the region vulnerable to supply and weather shocks.
Japanese policy authorities are focused on limiting Yen depreciation.
China trade surplus growing, supporting CNY appreciation.
Exhibit 6 annotations mark a ceasefire announcement, an MoU signing, a Houthi blockade announcement and US midterms as drivers of the Brent risk premium.

tension_points.bull_case: AI investment and earnings stay firmly positive in 2027 (S&P 500 EPS growth 11%), and gains pass to hyperscalers, AI users and non-AI companies as capital crowding out eases.
tension_points.bear_case: The second-derivative peak ends positive surprises, and markets look ahead to the 2028 investment peak. A slow rotation or tighter financial conditions could turn it into a larger aggregate shock.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Slow handoff to other sectors or accelerating feedback from financial and credit conditions would invalidate the smooth-rotation view.

tension_points.bull_case: Baseline is a gradual decline in energy prices with supply largely restored, and faster resolution in Iran or Ukraine would support bonds and equities.
tension_points.bear_case: Escalation in the Iran war or new supply disruptions would spike oil, hurting equities and bonds together.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Broadening of the conflict and new supply disruptions would invalidate the gradual-decline baseline.

tension_points.bull_case: Balance sheets of major borrowers are strong and the broader corporate sector is balanced, so base-case widening is modest.
tension_points.bear_case: Record AI-related issuance needs discounted pricing, and weaker economic conditions or AI profitability doubts could widen spreads more.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Economic conditions deteriorating by more than GS expects, or investor discomfort with AI investment profitability, would push spreads wider than the modest baseline.
